## What this week is for

Weeks 1–7 are not seven topics. They are one argument, and the midterm tests whether you
can see it:

> Success is contested and multidimensional (W1), which is why you have to read a standard
> for its *shape* rather than its checklist (W2), which is why selection is a judgement about
> criteria and not only a calculation (W3), which is why scope has to be decomposed before it
> can be scheduled (W4), which is what makes a critical path meaningful (W5), which is what
> makes crashing an economic decision rather than an arithmetic one (W6), which is why an
> estimate's accuracy is a function of design maturity rather than estimator effort (W7).

Tuesday is spent walking that chain in both directions, with the quantitative pieces re-worked
on the board. Bring the problems you got wrong.

## Midterm — Thursday 15 October, in class

::: {.callout-important}
## Format
75 minutes. **Closed book, closed notes. No computers, tablets, or phones.** A non-programmable
calculator is permitted and recommended. One double-sided page of hand-written notes is **not**
permitted — the point of this exam is what you can reason through unaided.
:::

**Covers** Weeks 1–7. Earned value (Week 9) is *not* on the midterm.

**Shape of the paper**

| Part | Weight | What it asks |
|:--|--:|:--|
| A · Short concept | 30% | Definitions, distinctions, and *why* a distinction matters. Expect "name three ways the iron triangle misleads." |
| B · Quantitative | 45% | A CPM network with a full float table; a crash step; a three-point estimate. Arithmetic is checkable — method is what earns marks. |
| C · Judgement | 25% | A short scenario. Choose, and defend the choice against the strongest alternative. There is more than one defensible answer; there are many indefensible ones. |

: {tbl-colwidths="[26,12,62]"}

**How to prepare.** Re-work the studio problems without the key, then check. Use the
[retrieval Tutor prompt](../ai.qmd#tutor) for mixed questions across all seven weeks —
mixing is what makes retrieval practice work, and it is the one form of AI use that helps
you on a closed-book exam.

**What is not tested.** Memorized process catalogues, ITTO tables, or standard edition numbers.
If it is the kind of thing you would look up in thirty seconds on the job, it is not on the paper.
